subject: psychology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In social learning theory, being rewarded for behaviour seen in others is called what?
questions.explain: Vicarious reinforcement is learning to repeat behaviour because we see it rewarded in others.

questions.q: Which of these aims mainly to change behaviour and reintegrate an offender rather than just punish?
questions.explain: Rehabilitation aims to reform offenders and help them reintegrate, reducing future offending.

questions.q: Differences in brain structure and function feature in which type of explanation of crime?
questions.explain: Differences in brain structure and function are part of biological explanations of criminal behaviour.

questions.q: Social learning theory explains criminal behaviour as being learned through what?
questions.explain: Social learning theory says criminal behaviour can be learned by observing and imitating role models.

questions.q: What is the difference between crime and deviance?
options: Crime breaks the law; deviance breaks social norms
questions.explain: Crime is behaviour that breaks the law, while deviance is behaviour that goes against social norms.

questions.q: Punishment is intended to reduce criminal behaviour mainly by doing what?
questions.explain: Punishment aims to deter offending by making the consequences of crime unpleasant.

questions.q: A behaviour can be deviant but not criminal. Which is the best example?
options: Talking loudly to yourself in public
questions.explain: Talking loudly to yourself breaks social norms (deviant) but is not against the law (not criminal).

questions.q: A criticism of using punishment alone to reduce crime is that it may do what?
options: Fail to teach better behaviour and cause resentment
questions.explain: Punishment alone may not teach alternative behaviour and can lead to resentment or further offending.

questions.q: A biological explanation of criminality suggests crime may be linked to what?
questions.explain: Biological explanations link criminality to inherited genes and differences in brain structure or function.

questions.q: Bandura's Bobo doll study is often used to support which explanation of aggression and crime?
questions.explain: Bandura's Bobo doll study showed children imitate aggression they observe, supporting social learning theory.

questions.q: Anger-management programmes try to reduce reoffending by doing what?
options: Teaching offenders to control emotional responses
questions.explain: Anger management teaches offenders to recognise and control emotional triggers, reducing reoffending.

questions.q: Token economy programmes used with offenders are based on which principle?
questions.explain: Token economies reward desired behaviour with tokens that can be exchanged for privileges, reinforcing good conduct.
